h1: The 6 Best Electric Pruning Shears for Vines of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Electric Pruners for Vines: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 electric pruning shears for vines, scored on cut capacity, cuts per charge, weight and battery, from WORKPRO to KOMOK.
summary: The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is the best electric pruner for vines: a listed 900 cuts per charge, tool-free blade changes and a battery and charger in the box. The SEESII 1.4-inch brushless is the stronger cutter for old, woody stems. The KOMOK 1.2-inch brings two batteries for long sessions, and the WORKPRO 0.8-inch is the cheap, light option for fresh green growth.
intro: Vine pruning is the opposite of felling a tree. You are not making a few big cuts, you are making hundreds of small ones, up a trellis, along a wire, above your head, with a tangle of stems pulling the other way. Buyers shop for maximum cutting diameter and then discover the real limit is arm fatigue and a battery that quits halfway through the row.

So we ranked these six electric pruners on endurance and handling first, then capacity. We reviewed spec sheets and owner feedback for cutting diameter, cuts per charge, weight, battery supply and blade access, then scored each on the Primea framework. Vines rarely need more than an inch of cut, so a bigger jaw only earns points when it does not cost handling.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX Cordless Pruner Electric Pruning Shears, Battery and Charger Included, 900 Cuts Per Charge
products.verdict: The only pruner here that states cuts per charge, built for repeat small cuts.
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's 20V MAX pruner lists 900 cuts per charge, ships with its battery and charger, and uses a tool-free blade change. Vine work is repetition, so a stated cut count is the most useful number a listing can give.

It leads because it answers the question vine growers actually ask: will it last the row? The KOMOK models list 8 to 10 hours of runtime, but those figures are looser than a cut count. Against the SEESII, you give up the larger jaw and brushless motor for a proven brand ecosystem and quick blade swaps, which matter when sap gums up a blade.

Buy it for trellised grapes, climbing roses and similar thin growth. The caveat is that the listing gives no cutting diameter, so confirm capacity against your thickest stems.
products.idealFor: Growers making hundreds of thin cuts along trellises and wires.
products.skipIf: Your vines are thick and woody and need a confirmed wide jaw.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Cordless Pruner for Gardening
products.verdict: A brushless 1.4-inch pruner for old woody vines, at a modest price.
products.description:
The SEESII combines a 1.4-inch cutting diameter with a brushless motor. For woody vines such as mature grape or wisteria canes, that capacity lets you cut a stem in one pass instead of rocking and twisting.

It ranks second because the listing gives no cut count or battery detail, where the BLACK+DECKER names 900 cuts per charge. Against the identical-diameter Upgraded model, the SEESII leaves out the LCD, but at the same price bracket it is the simpler tool with fewer things to go wrong in the damp. Brushless motors run cooler under repeated cuts, which suits long pruning days.

Buy it if your vines have thick old growth. The caveat is that endurance is unconfirmed, so keep a spare battery in mind for long rows.
products.idealFor: Owners of mature, woody vines that need a one-pass cut.
products.skipIf: You want a confirmed battery life figure before buying.

products.name: Upgraded Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Diameter Cordless Power Pruner with LCD Display, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: The SEESII's spec, plus an LCD that tells you what the battery is doing.
products.description:
This Upgraded pruner matches the SEESII on a 1.4-inch cutting diameter and brushless motor, and adds an LCD display. On a long vine row, a readout that shows battery level beats guessing when the blades will stall.

It sits third purely on a judgment call. The LCD is helpful information, but it is also another component that can fail on a wet trellis, and the extra feature does not change cutting ability. The SEESII does the same cutting for the same bracket. Against the BLACK+DECKER, it offers a bigger jaw but no stated cuts per charge.

Buy it if you want to see battery status before the shears quit mid-stem. The caveat is the generic listing: with no brand name, support depends entirely on the seller.
products.idealFor: Growers who want to see battery level before a long row.
products.skipIf: You prefer a simpler tool or a named brand with support.

products.name: KOMOK Electric Pruning Shears, Cordless Electric Pruner Battery Operated Tree Branch Cutter, 1.2 inch (30mm) Cutting Diameter
products.verdict: Two 2Ah batteries and an 8 to 10 hour runtime for all-day pruning.
products.description:
The KOMOK pruner offers a 1.2-inch (30mm) cutting diameter, ships with two 2Ah batteries and lists an 8 to 10 hour runtime. Two packs means you can swap and keep working while the spare charges.

It ranks fourth because the price bracket is $100 to $200, which is more than the SEESII and Upgraded models for a smaller jaw. Against the BLACK+DECKER, the runtime claim is looser than 900 specific cuts. What you buy here is continuity: a second battery for a large vineyard row or an overgrown fence.

Buy it for a big planting where one battery will not finish the job. The caveat is cost and weight: it asks for roughly double the budget of the two 1.4-inch picks without a larger cut.
products.idealFor: Large plantings or vineyard rows where one battery would not finish.
products.skipIf: You prune a small trellis and do not need a second battery.

products.name: Kebtek Cordless Pruning Shears 25MM Electric Pruners 880G Lightweight
products.verdict: A named 880g weight and 25mm cut, for overhead trellis work.
products.description:
The Kebtek pruner lists a 25mm cutting diameter and an 880g weight. On a vine, weight is felt overhead and at arm's length, so a stated figure helps you compare against the others, which mostly omit it.

It ranks fifth because the price bracket is $100 to $200 and the listing gives no battery or runtime detail. Against the KOMOK in the same bracket, you get a similar-size cut but no two-battery supply or runtime claim. 880g is workable for a morning of pruning, but not light enough that fatigue disappears over a long vineyard row.

Buy it if weight is your priority and you will check the battery specs before ordering. The caveat is the missing battery information, which is the biggest unknown on a vine-pruning tool.
products.idealFor: Overhead trellis work where a known weight helps you plan fatigue.
products.skipIf: You need battery life confirmed or want the lowest price.

products.name: WORKPRO 7.2V Electric Pruning Shears, 0.8" Cutting Diameter
products.verdict: A 0.8-inch, 7.2V pruner for fresh vine shoots and tendrils, nothing thicker.
products.description:
The WORKPRO lists a 0.8-inch cutting diameter and a 7.2V motor, in the $25 to $50 bracket. For soft green growth, tendrils and the current season's shoots, that capacity covers nearly all of the cutting a vine needs.

It ranks last because the jaw is the smallest here: next to the 1.4-inch SEESII, it stops short on older canes. A 7.2V system also has less headroom than 20V MAX, so expect it to slow down sooner on tougher stems. But for light summer training, it is the cheapest way to avoid hand cramps.

Buy it for thin, fresh growth and small hands. The caveat is the winter prune: dormant, lignified canes are the cut this tool is least suited to.
products.idealFor: Summer training of thin, fresh vine growth.
products.skipIf: You do winter pruning on old, woody canes.

whatMatters.detail: A vine row can mean hundreds of cuts, and a pruner that quits halfway wastes the afternoon. A stated figure, like the BLACK+DECKER's 900 cuts, is more useful than a vague runtime in hours. If a listing offers neither, treat endurance as unknown and plan for a spare battery.

Diameter is the thickest stem the blade will cut cleanly. Summer vine shoots are thin, but old canes can reach an inch or more. Measure your thickest stem with a ruler, then choose a jaw at least a quarter inch larger, so the motor never labors.

Arm fatigue is the real limit on overhead trellis work. Every ounce is multiplied by hundreds of lifts. The Kebtek lists 880g, which most rivals omit. If a listing does not give weight, check the photos for hand size and the battery location.

A second battery turns a one-hour tool into an all-day tool. The KOMOK ships with two 2Ah packs, and the BLACK+DECKER includes one with a charger. Count the batteries in the box, and note whether a charger is listed, since some bare tools omit it.

Sap and plant juices gum blades, and a dull or sticky blade cuts ragged and stresses the vine. Tool-free blade changes, listed on the BLACK+DECKER, let you swap in seconds. Check the listing for the words tool-free or spare blades.

faq.q: Can the WORKPRO cut dormant grape canes?
faq.a: It lists a 0.8-inch cutting diameter and a 7.2V motor, so thin canes are within reach but old lignified wood is not. For dormant pruning, step up to the 1.4-inch SEESII or Upgraded model.

faq.q: Is the BLACK+DECKER's battery shared with other tools?
faq.a: It uses a 20V MAX battery, which the brand uses across other tools, but check compatibility on the product page before assuming a swap works. The listing confirms the battery and charger are included with the pruner.

faq.q: Is the KOMOK worth over the SEESII?
faq.a: Only if you need two batteries. The KOMOK costs more for a smaller 1.2-inch jaw, while the SEESII gives 1.4 inches in a brushless body. Choose KOMOK for endurance on big plantings, SEESII for capacity on a budget.

faq.q: How do I keep sap off the blades?
faq.a: Wipe the blade with rubbing alcohol after each session. On the BLACK+DECKER, the tool-free change makes swapping a dull blade fast. Sticky blades cut ragged and can tear the vine, so clean them before storing.

faq.q: How should I store the batteries?
faq.a: Take the battery off the pruner, store it indoors partly charged, and keep it away from freezing sheds. This matters most with the KOMOK, whose spare pack otherwise sits idle for months.

faq.q: Can electric pruners cut wire trellis ties?
faq.a: Avoid it. Metal wire damages the blade on any of these, from the 0.8-inch WORKPRO to the 25mm Kebtek. Remove ties by hand before cutting, or you will dull the edge in minutes.

finalTake: For most vine growers the BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is the best buy: a stated 900 cuts per charge, a battery and charger in the box, and tool-free blade changes. For old woody canes, step up to the SEESII 1.4-inch brushless. A large planting calls for the KOMOK with its two batteries, and the WORKPRO suits light summer training on a tight budget.
